definition: Bladder reflex refers to the automatic nerve-controlled activity that produces bladder contractions. In this source, it specifically means spontaneous bladder contractions that can vary from regular to chaotic patterns and can be suppressed or stabilized by sacral spinal stimulation.

reasons: The phrase “automatic nerve-controlled activity” is a generalization not stated in the packet; the source only supports spontaneous bladder reflexes/contractions.
“Sacral spinal stimulation” is broader than the packet’s specific intervention, sacral intraspinal microstimulation targeting the dorsal horn of the S2 spinal cord.
The source supports suppression/stabilization of bladder reflex dynamics by that specific stimulation, but not the definition’s broader formulation as a general property of the term.

The definition’s phrase “automatic nerve-controlled activity” is not explicitly stated in the packet; the packet discusses bladder reflexes and their suppression/modulation via nerve stimulation but does not define them as “automatic nerve-controlled activity.”

The remaining elements (spontaneous bladder contractions varying from regular to chaotic patterns, and suppression/stabilization by sacral intraspinal microstimulation targeting S2 dorsal horn) are supported by the packet.
